text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: High error rate & latency for org `apexly` detected (QPS spike) — automatic page sent to on-call. See graphs: https://dash.redwood.example/apexly/spike

maya_oncall: I got the page, stepping in. ETA 2m to confirm metrics.

devin_sre: ping — I'm around if you want a hand with rate-limiter rules.

maya_oncall: Verified 5xx increase and tail latency up. Root cause looks like sudden traffic burst from a new customer campaign. Current org QPS 6x baseline.

ops-automation: Autoscaling triggered but backend queueing causing KV cache thrash. Recommending immediate soft-rate-limit for apexly to protect cluster.

maya_oncall: Agreed. Plan: apply emergency org throttle to 150 req/s (was 1200), enable grace tokens for premium flows, message support to inform customer. Will monitor.

devin_sre: Command I'll run on rate-limiter gateway:
```
# emergency rule
redwood-ctl rl create --org apexly --limit 150 --burst 300 --reason "emergency spike 1768456789"
```

maya_oncall: Running now.

ops-automation: rule applied in 8s, propagation to edge ~12s. Logs: `rl-service: rule=apexly emergency applied by maya_oncall`

leo_support: Pinging account team and CS to prep message. Draft: "We've applied a temporary protection on your account to stabilize service while we investigate. We'll follow up in 15 minutes." OK to send?

maya_oncall: Send after we confirm stability + a quick rollback play if customer is blocked.

devin_sre: Seeing 5xx drop by ~70% and P95 latency down 40% within 90s. Good signal.

ops-automation: Also disabled non-critical streaming feature flag for apexly (ff.apexly.streams=false) to cut noisy tails. Trigger: `feature-toggle set apexly streams false --by maya_oncall`

maya_oncall: Confirmed feature toggle successful.

leo_support: Sent customer note (cc:account): "Temporary protections are active to stabilize service. We're monitoring and will update shortly." They replied: "Thanks, please keep us posted."

sarah_prodeng: Quick note — this client runs long context workloads; can we add a temporary lower token-per-request cap to reduce KV pressure?

devin_sre: Good call. Applied token cap via rate-limiter header rewrite: `x-rl-token-cap=4096` for apexly.

maya_oncall: Metrics holding steady for 6m. Gradual rollout: keep emergency throttle for now, re-evaluate in 20m for step-up if stable.

leo_support: Marking incident as customer-impacting but mitigated. Planning status update to ops@ and account team.

devin_sre: Logging remediation in incident runbook. Will snapshot config: `rl-service rules show --org apexly > /var/tmp/apexly-rule-1768456789.log`

maya_oncall: On-call handoff at 23:00 UTC to devin_sre. Leaving notes: applied emergency rl, disabled streams ff, token cap set, customer notified.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation in place. Incident severity reduced to SEV-2. Please update pager duty ticket PD-4829 and attach logs.

maya_oncall: Thanks team, I'll follow up with a short postmortem and recommended durable fixes (quota bump request, workload guidance for customer, defensive auto-throttle).

devin_sre: I'll cover the overnight watch. If anything regresses, escalate back to prod-eng.

leo_support: Noted. Closing thread once PD updated. :thumbsup:
